final_verdict: the attention backward is correct; attention has a real, architecture-specific mantissa-precision requirement that the convolution does not

bmm_backward_shared_isolated.setup: B=1 T=4 D=3, saturation off, 50-bit mantissa, no ReLU, autograd reference
bmm_backward_shared_isolated.verdict: K branch already aligns BEFORE the reduction; the hypothesised reduction-axis shift bug is not present

full_block_cosine_vs_autograd.verdict: the earlier low/erratic cosines were a TEST artefact: the integer path masks on a 7-bit quantised S while the float reference masked on the exact S, and that mismatch is independent of hidden_bits so it never shrank

attn_hb16.verdict: does learn - train and test both rise and track each other - but plateaus far below conv, and part of the hinge reduction is logit shrinkage (std 56 -> 27) rather than classification

ruled_out_for_attention: score nonlinearity (ReLU / leaky k=3 / linear all at chance at hb=8)
corrections_made_during_this_investigati: 'dead gradient, not a direction error' - over-stated: at hb=16 the gradient is dense and the model does learn, slowly
'formula error in the Q/K path' - WRONG, it was my float reference using an unquantised ReLU mask
the user's hypothesised reduction-axis shift bug in the K branch - not present, verified cos=1.000000 in isolation
standing_result: conv learns at 8-bit gradient mantissa; attention needs >=12-16 bits before its gradient survives at all. That is an attention-specific precision requirement, not an implementation bug.
